en.headline: Woman loses nearly HK$69 million to scammers posing as mainland officials
en.dek: A 43-year-old Hong Kong woman transferred about HK$68.9 million over a month after callers claiming to be mainland law-enforcement officers accused her of a crime and demanded money to prove her innocence.
body: Police said a 43-year-old woman reported that she had been defrauded of approximately HK$68.9 million by people posing as mainland Chinese law-enforcement officers. The victim received calls accusing her of involvement in a crime and was told to transfer funds as a guarantee of her innocence.

Between 2 July and 1 August she made multiple transfers, reported as 81 separate payments into ten designated local bank accounts. She contacted police on Wednesday after becoming suspicious and discussing the matter with her family.

The case has been classified as obtaining property by deception and is being investigated by the Western District crime squad. No arrests have been made. Police reiterated that such offences carry a maximum penalty of 14 years’ imprisonment and urged the public to remain vigilant against fake-official phone scams.

zh.headline: 女子墮假冒內地官員騙局 損失近6,900萬元
zh.dek: 一名43歲香港女子接獲自稱內地執法人員來電，指她涉案並要求轉帳「保證金」，一個月內合共轉出約6,890萬元至指定帳戶。
body: 警方表示，一名43歲女子報稱接獲自稱內地執法人員的電話，指她涉及罪案，並要求她轉帳金錢以證明清白，其後發現被騙約6,890萬元。
事主於7月2日至8月1日期間，按指示分81次將款項轉入10個本地銀行帳戶。她周三與家人傾談後起疑，遂報警求助。
案件列作以欺騙手段取得財產，交由西區刑事調查隊跟進，暫時無人被捕。警方提醒公眾慎防假冒官員電話騙案，有關罪行最高可判監禁14年。
